We started seeing a sudden rise in 5xx responses and recurrent timeouts from requests routed to model polarix4b (endpoint: /v1/models/polarix4b/generate) around 08:30 PT. Impact: multiple downstream dashboards failing, about 12% request error-rate over the last 20 minutes. Request IDs attached in polarix_error_logs.zip.

Can you confirm whether this is a known degradation and whether there's an ETA for mitigation? We're on a critical release and this is blocking a canary.

Thanks,

On Mon, Jul 19, 2026 at 09:12 Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — adding the on-call ops notes below and opening a short bridge.

Joined bridge. Quick findings so far:
- One serving pool (pool-px-3) began returning 503s when tail latency spiked > 1.6s; CPU and GPU utilization on that pool are normal.
- KV cache miss rate on polarix4b increased 10x for requests with long-prefixes (>1024 tokens).
- We observed a pattern of repeated full KV cache invalidations on pool-px-3 between 08:29–08:36 UTC (attached timeline).

Next steps: pin traffic away from pool-px-3, enable per-request shorter-prefix fallback (truncate to 1024 tokens) for highly-weighted routes, and push a config that increases cache retention temporarily.

Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-19T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike of 5xx from Polarix4b affecting production dashboards

Confirmed from model side: around the window we saw a kernel fallback on optimized attention path for polarix4b on pool-px-3. That fallback path increases memory churn and triggers a periodic GC that can cause timeouts under certain prefix distributions. No code rollout at that time — likely a latent regression in kernel selection heuristics triggered by long-context requests.

I've pushed a hotpatch to bias kernel selection away from the fallback on pool-px-3 and increased cache TTL. Will monitor.

Stephanie Nguyen
Applied ML / Inference Runtime

Subject: Re: Spike of 5xx from Polarix4b affecting production dashboards

Hi Alex — quick update from our ops team: we identified a model-kernel selection fallback that became pathological for long-prefix requests on one serving pool (pool-px-3). We routed traffic away from that pool and deployed a conservative kernel bias and cache TTL increase at ~09:40 PT.

Current status: error rate for your traffic is down from ~12% to ~1.1% in the last 20 minutes; we continue to monitor while retaining the conservative config. We have not observed a correlated increase in latency for your successful requests.

Attachments included: polarix_error_logs.zip (subset of request IDs you sent), polarix-timeline-UTC-20260719.csv (internal timeline).

Proposed follow-ups:
1) Short postmortem and timeline sent by Thursday 2026-07-22 with root cause and permanent mitigations.
2) Option for Nimbus to whitelist a reserve fallback model (polarix-stable-ql) for critical routes for immediate guaranteed SLA — can schedule a quick config if you want.

Please confirm if you want us to enable the reserve fallback for your canary traffic.

Thanks for the patience — sincerely sorry for the disruption.

Mina Haddad
Program Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
